narrative.text: Wetter than normal conditions expected over most parts of Ethiopia, parts of northern and central and southern Somalia, northern Eritrea, South Sudan, central to southern Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, and Tanzania.

Normal to drier than normal conditions are expected over western and northern Kenya, western and eastern Uganda, south-western to central and north-eastern Ethiopia, Djibouti, western South Sudan and most parts of Somalia.

summary.title: Robustness of the extraction
summary.text: With the ICPAC map as digitized and shifted by one source pixel in each direction, the All Ethiopia category agreement stays between 53.8% and 54.7%. With the ICPAC map as digitized and shifted by one source pixel in each direction, the FMAM rainfall contribution domain category agreement stays between 54.8% and 55.4%. With the ICPAC map as digitized and shifted by one source pixel in each direction, the FMAM main-season rainfall domain (Belg / Gu / Ganna, >=40% of annual) category agreement stays between 52.1% and 53.6%. These are bounded sensitivity checks of the extraction, not statistical confidence intervals; exact EMI zone comparisons remain unavailable.

paragraphs.text: The platform does not show a unique favoured category over EMI zone West under its applicable rule. EMI prints 25% / 30% / 45% (below / near / above). Over the whole zone (as digitized from the EMI figure), the platform area mean is 31% / 34% / 35%: no clear category in one source.

Both outlooks favour wetter-than-normal conditions over EMI zone North-central. EMI prints 10% / 30% / 60% (below / near / above). Over the whole zone (as digitized from the EMI figure), the platform area mean is 25% / 34% / 41%: same category.

Both outlooks favour wetter-than-normal conditions over EMI zone South-central. EMI prints 15% / 30% / 55% (below / near / above). Over the whole zone (as digitized from the EMI figure), the platform area mean is 22% / 33% / 45%: same category.

Both outlooks favour wetter-than-normal conditions over EMI zone Southeast. EMI prints 20% / 35% / 45% (below / near / above). Over the whole zone (as digitized from the EMI figure), the platform area mean is 19% / 29% / 52%: same category.

The EMI zones were digitized from the figure's fill colours and placed by fitting the country outline, so their boundaries are approximate; the figure states no reference period, so probability differences are not calculated.

The outlooks favour different categories over much of their shared displayed area in Ethiopia. ICPAC shows a favoured category on 89% of Ethiopia and no forecast category shown (the legend does not explain the grey areas) on 11%; where it shows one it favours above normal on 68%, most often at 40-50% and 33-40%. The platform favours above normal on 57% and below normal on 8% of Ethiopia. There is category agreement of 54.2% within the compared area, which covers 68% of the analysed national area; opposite categories (above vs below) on 10% of the compared area. ICPAC publishes only the favoured category and its probability interval, so probabilities are not differenced. The official outlook covers Mar 2026–May 2026 and the platform Feb 2026–May 2026 (Feb 2026 only in the platform), so this compares spatial tendencies, not probabilities for the same seasonal event.

The outlooks favour different categories over much of their shared displayed area in the FMAM rainfall contribution domain. ICPAC shows a favoured category on >99% of the FMAM rainfall contribution domain and no forecast category shown (the legend does not explain the grey areas) on <1%; where it shows one it favours above normal on 66%, most often at 40-50% and 33-40%. The platform favours above normal on 70% and below normal on 2% of the FMAM rainfall contribution domain. There is category agreement of 55.1% within the compared area, which covers 82% of the analysed domain; opposite categories (above vs below) on 9% of the compared area. ICPAC publishes only the favoured category and its probability interval, so probabilities are not differenced. The official outlook covers Mar 2026–May 2026 and the platform Feb 2026–May 2026 (Feb 2026 only in the platform), so this compares spatial tendencies, not probabilities for the same seasonal event.

paragraphs.area: FMAM main-season rainfall domain (Belg / Gu / Ganna, >=40% of annual)
paragraphs.text: The outlooks favour different categories over much of their shared displayed area in the FMAM main-season rainfall domain (Belg / Gu / Ganna, >=40% of annual). ICPAC shows a favoured category on 100% of the FMAM main-season rainfall domain (Belg / Gu / Ganna, >=40% of annual) and no forecast category shown (the legend does not explain the grey areas) on 0%; where it shows one it favours above normal on 51%, most often at 40-50% and 33-40%. The platform favours above normal on 93% and below normal on 0% of the FMAM main-season rainfall domain (Belg / Gu / Ganna, >=40% of annual). There is category agreement of 52.7% within the compared area, which covers 97% of the analysed domain; opposite categories (above vs below) on 12% of the compared area. ICPAC publishes only the favoured category and its probability interval, so probabilities are not differenced. The official outlook covers Mar 2026–May 2026 and the platform Feb 2026–May 2026 (Feb 2026 only in the platform), so this compares spatial tendencies, not probabilities for the same seasonal event.

Not calculated: rainfall-anomaly differences, because no official rainfall-amount anomaly product was found in the checked ICPAC and EMI products; same-event probability differences, because the target windows or spatial supports differ and ICPAC publishes only favoured-category intervals.
Single-season performance against CHIRPS observations is now evaluated (see Against CHIRPS observations). One season does not establish that any provider, or the platform, is generally more skilful.

observed.name: observed_comparison.png
notes: Single season: descriptive scores for one year, not evidence of general skill.
Each outlook is scored against observations for its own target window; the observed tercile uses CHIRPS 1993-2025 terciles per 0.25° cell (official reference periods are not stated).

Favoured category: for the platform and EMI, the untied leading tercile where it reaches 40% (the map display rule); for ICPAC, the dominant category ICPAC printed, including its 33–40% intervals (the share resting on 33–40% is reported). "Chance" is the climatological probability of the favoured category over the same cells (about one in three).

Coverage: observation coverage is the share of the area with usable CHIRPS observations; outlook coverage the share of those cells where the provider issued an outlook (ICPAC grey areas and EMI's excluded dry areas have none); favoured-category coverage the share where its rule selects a category. Match percentages are within the favoured cells.
RPSS: ranked probability skill score against the CHIRPS climatology, on identical cells; ICPAC publishes only the favoured category and its interval, so no RPSS is computed for ICPAC.
EMI zone probabilities are applied uniformly over each digitized zone.

windows.Mar 2026, Apr 2026, May 2026: sum of verified monthly totals (Mar, Apr, May); terciles from the same months 1993-2025
